bank-ex92.title: Ex 9.2: how fast must the op amp be to settle in 5 ns?

steps.title: 1% settling takes ln(100) = 4.6 time constants
τ = 1/(β·ωu), so ωu ≥ ln(1/ε)/(β·t)
Divide by 2π

hints: Settling is exponential with τ = Aclosed/ωu.
How many τ for 1%?
t = τ·ln(1/ε); ωu = Aclosed·ln(1/ε)/t.

Walk the bias string: R2 from VGS7 up to VG4, R1 from VG4 up to M8’s drain (VDD − |VGS8|)
R1: from VG4 up to M8’s drain

bank-t5q2.title: Tutorial 5 Q2: which pair for the CMFB amplifier, and the loop gain
bank-t5q2.statement: In the folded cascode with resistive sensing (R1, R2), an error amplifier compares Vout,CM with VREF and drives M3, M4 through VE. The error amplifier is a differential pair with an active current-mirror load. (a) NMOS or PMOS input pair? (b) Which expression is the CMFB loop gain?

unknowns.label: (a) Input pair of the error amplifier
choices: PMOS: its mirror output sits near VGS,n, the level M3, M4 need
NMOS: its mirror output sits near VDD − |VGS,p|

steps.title: (a) VE must sit at about VGS3 (≈ Vthn + Vov), low. A PMOS pair with an NMOS mirror puts its output one VGS,n above ground: the right level. An NMOS pair’s output sits near VDD − |VGS,p|, far too high
(b) Go round the loop: Vout,CM → (sense: gain 1) → error amp A_EA = gm,EA(rO,N ‖ rO,P) → VE → M3, M4 (gm3 each) → a CM current into each output
In CM no current flows through R1, R2 (both ends move together), so each output sees Rup ‖ Rdown

hints: What DC level must VE have to bias M3, M4?
Where does the output of a 5-T OTA sit, for each pair type?
Break the loop at VE and go round: sense, amplify, convert to current, back to voltage.
In common mode, R1 and R2 carry no current.
flags: Razavi 9.12 gives no device sizes, so (b) is asked as an expression. The loop is negative: Vout,CM up → VE up → more current in M3, M4 → outputs pulled down.

bank-t5q3.title: Tutorial 5 Q3: CM gain and CMRR with and without CMFB
bank-t5q3.statement: I1 = 50 µA, I2 = 200 µA, W/L = 50 µm/1 µm for every device, R = 10 MΩ. VDD = 1.8 V, µnCox = 100 µA/V², µpCox = 50 µA/V², λp = 0.2 V⁻¹, λn = 0.1 V⁻¹, Vthn = 0.4 V, |Vthp| = 0.5 V. Without CMFB: Ad, ACM, the optimum VO,CM and CMRR. With CMFB: the CM gain needed for ±1% on VO,CM, the CM loop gain, the CM gain achieved and the CMRR.

steps.title: Currents: M3, M4 copy I1 (50 µA each), so M5 carries 100 µA; M11 copies I2, 100 µA in each of M7, M8
Differential: the R midpoint is AC ground, so each output sees rO1 ‖ rO3 ‖ R
Common mode: no current in the R’s; CM half circuit with 2rO5 in the source
Output range: Vov5 + Vov1 up to VDD − |Vov3|; the optimum CM is its middle
CMRR = Ad/|ACM|
±1%: the output CM may move 2·1%·VO,CM while the input CM sweeps its whole range (Vov5 + VGS1 up to VO,CM + Vth1)
Loop: ΔVO,CM → M8 (gm7/2 of pair current) → diode M9 (1/gm9 ‖ rO9 ‖ rO7) → M5 (gm5) → half per side into rO3 ‖ Rdown,CM
Feedback divides the CM gain by (1 + T); Ad is unchanged
CMRR with CMFB (the circuit does not reach the 0.010 target)

hints: Find every current from the mirrors first.
In DM the R midpoint is AC ground; in CM no current flows in the R’s.
CM half circuit: the tail counts as 2rO5.
flags: Tutorials 4–6 have no answer key. These numbers come from the engine with the assumptions listed; check them against your class solution.

This exact question is the 2024-25 mid-sem Q1, and its key fixes the readings used here: VO,CM = middle of [Vov5 + Vov1, VDD − |Vov3|] = 0.97 V; ACM,req = 2·1%·VO,CM/(Vin,CM range) = 0.031; ACM ≈ rO3/(2rO5) = 0.5.

The key’s loop gain (55.7, so ACM,f = 0.0088 and CMRR 5373) uses gm10 = 0.316 mS, but √(2·100µ·50·100µ) = 1 mS. With 1 mS the loop gain is ≈ 17, as below. If your instructor insists on 55.7, that slip is the reason.
